newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SMH sees 1996 profit rise, sales up 5-7 pct.
newsitem.headline: SMH sees 1996 profit rise, sales up 5-7 pct.

text.p: Swiss watchmaker Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horlogerie (SMH) will certainly post better earnings in 1996 than in 1995, chairman Nicolas Hayek said on Tuesday.
He also told reporters he saw sales rising five to seven percent in 1996.
"We certainly will be better than last year," he said when asked about the 1996 earnings outlook.
"SMH sales will this year go up five to seven percent," he said, adding: "The next year we expect to be much higher."

SMH, whose products range from luxury Blancpain watches to plastic SWATCH timepieces, saw net profit fall 13 percent last year to 273 million Swiss francs. Sales slipped one percent to 2.64 billion francs, hurt by the strong Swiss franc.

Hayek noted that Christmas season sales in December made up 15 to 20 percent of annual turnover, but added business was going very well in the United States, Britain and Japan so that total sales should be around the good levels of 1992 and 1993.
"We think we will have a good year," he said. Sales in October hit a monthly record.
